nodes.name: Desktop running mihomo
nodes.notes: The machine that runs the mihomo core. Its worker runs here as observer desktop, so the core's external controller stays on literal loopback and is never exposed to the network.

nodes.name: Proxy exit
nodes.notes: The upstream node the root group is expected to select. Topophany reads the selection the core reports; it never edits the configuration or switches a group.

nodes.name: Application host
nodes.notes: Where the application reached through the proxy runs.

observers.name: Desktop worker
observers.context: native process on the machine running the mihomo core; reads its controller over loopback

endpoints.notes: The core's external-controller, bound to 127.0.0.1:9090. Its secret is read from the environment variable named by the check's adapter.token_env, never from this file.
Replace with an application health URL that is meant to be reached through the proxy.

services.name: Application through mihomo
services.notes: Its availability comes from the application check's HTTP response through the core's listener, never from the controller's report.

paths.name: through the local mihomo listener
paths.notes: The core's own mixed-port listener on loopback, dialed as one SOCKS5 hop. The hops inside the core belong to it and are not decomposed; a declared route is not proof of a request's path.

checks.name: mihomo reported runtime
checks.notes: Reads only /configs, /proxies and /providers/proxies from the controller; delay tests are never triggered. root_proxy names the selector group whose selection is resolved, and expected_mode and expected_tun assert what the core reports: set expected_tun to false when the core runs as a system proxy without TUN. This is reported runtime state, not proof that application traffic followed that route: a reported mode, TUN setting or selection never shows where a request went. Keep the separate application check (app-through-mihomo) for availability.

checks.name: application through mihomo
checks.notes: The application evidence: an HTTP response obtained through the core's listener, as this desktop's user enters the service (user_entry). It shows the application answered through the proxy, not which upstream node carried the request.
